summary: The R5 split does what was asked and nothing more. Stages S1-S3 of `produce_and_verify` moved into the new `run/producer.rs` as `run_baseline`, `prepare_producer` and `run_producer`, called in that order. The moved body text is the same as the removed text, except four `return Ok(Flow::Stop);` lines and one `&mut` that clippy required dropping; the CHANGELOG lists both. The driver turns `Flow::Stop` back into `return Ok(closing)`. No test line changed, and the test count is 627, as the CHANGELOG says. The CHANGELOG entry gives the early-return pairings with line numbers, the values carried between stages, the lines that are not moved text, and the caller counts, and my spot checks match it. Athena's own `cargo test --locked` was killed at its 900 s deadline. My two full runs (tasks bi1ojl6mh and b8zjjdtwv) both exited 0; I saw only the exit codes, because the output files are outside my working directory. The targeted runs passed: the R0 ordering test module (12 tests) and the 8 lifecycle producer tests. fmt and clippy passed in Athena's records. The findings left are minor: the design doc still says `Stage::Stop` where the code has `Flow::Stop`.
